claim_text: eNK -> dNK (menstrual cycle to pregnancy transition)

audit.primary_source_citation: Feyaerts D, Benner M, Comitini G, Shadmanfar W, van der Heijden OWH, Joosten I, van der Molen RG. "NK cell receptor profiling of endometrial and decidual NK cells reveals pregnancy-induced adaptations." Front Immunol. 2024;15:1353556. doi:10.3389/fimmu.2024.1353556. PMID 38571943 / PMC10987737. [Selected as primary because it is the only located primary paper whose stated aim is to test the eNK->dNK precursor proposition head-on in humans; full text and methods read and archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/S3_PMC10987737.txt and /home/user/aaa/refs/S3_PMC10987737_METHODS_verbatim.txt. Co-canonical human source Strunz B et al., Sci Immunol 2021;6(56):eabb7800, PMID 33617461, doi:10.1126/sciimmunol.abb7800 — closed access, methods NOT read (see fulltext_unavailable_reason). Supporting readable primaries: Whettlock EM et al., Front Immunol 2022;13:880438, PMID 35784314 / PMC9245422; Sojka DK et al., J Immunol 2018;201:2551-6, PMID 30275046 / PMC6552671 (mouse).]
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Feyaerts 2024 (designated primary) was obtained in full, including verbatim Materials and Methods. The co-canonical source the claim also rests on — Strunz et al. Sci Immunol 2021, eabb7800 — could NOT be read: Unpaywall reports oa_status "closed", is_oa false, has_repository_copy false, oa_locations []; the Europe PMC core record lists exactly one fullTextUrl with availability "Subscription required" and lit.py returns STATUS=ABSTRACT_ONLY; WebFetch of https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciimmunol.abb7800 returns HTTP 403; searches of KI/Cambridge repositories returned no deposited manuscript. I therefore did NOT paraphrase its abstract as methods. The only method-level facts I could verify for Strunz 2021 come from the authors' own deposited analysis repository (github.com/darogan/KI_Strunz_Bjorkstrom, ArrayExpress E-MTAB-8709): 12 BULK RNA-seq libraries from 4 uterine donors, sorted into CD39-KIR-, CD39-KIR+, CD39+KIR+ uNK (4 libraries each); the deposited pipeline is FastQC/STAR/featureCounts/DESeq2 with NO pseudotime, RNA-velocity or scRNA-seq step. So the "continuous differentiation pathway" in its title is an ordering of static sorted subsets by marker acquisition, not a tracked transition.
audit.species: Human (primary source and entire human evidence base). The only lineage-grade experiments bearing on the claim are in mouse (C57BL/6 Ncr1-iCre x Rosa-mT/mG parabionts, Sojka 2018; Rosa26-RFP x Tbx21-Cre fate map, Mohamed 2026 PMID 41782473).
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, in an unpaired cross-sectional design, surface NK-receptor repertoire (KIR2DL1/S1, KIR2DL2/L3/S2, KIR2DS1, KIR3DL1/S1, LILRB1, NKG2A, NKG2C, NKG2D, NKp30, NKp46, CD244) was measured by 10-colour flow cytometry on CD3-CD56+ cells, and 64 receptor co-expression subpopulations enumerated, in two separate donor groups: (a) endometrial NK cells recovered from MENSTRUAL BLOOD collected within the first 36 h of menstruation (n=26 healthy non-pregnant women; RosetteSep granulocyte depletion + Ficoll), used as a proxy for endometrium; and (b) decidual NK cells released from first-trimester decidual tissue at 6-15 weeks of elective termination (n=14 different women; Accutase/gentleMACS digestion + discontinuous Percoll). Group frequencies were compared. No woman contributed both an endometrial and a decidual sample; no cell, clone or donor was observed at more than one reproductive stage; no label, barcode, chimerism marker or proliferation readout was used. Supporting cross-sectional work is the same design: Whettlock 2022 measured uNK1/2/3 frequency, KIR2D/LILRB1/CD94 expression and PMA-ionomycin-induced CD107a/TNF/IFN-gamma/IL-8/GM-CSF at 7 reproductive stages in 29 endometrial Pipelle biopsies (8 menstrual, 7 proliferative, 10 secretory, 4 postpartum) plus 10 first-trimester and 16 term decidual samples, each stage from different women, integrated with four published scRNA-seq datasets (proliferative n=3, secretory n=3, first trimester n=5, second trimester n=1, third trimester n=3 donors).
audit.n: Primary (Feyaerts 2024): 26 menstrual-blood/endometrium donors + 14 first-trimester decidua donors = 40 total, 0 paired. Supporting (Whettlock 2022): 29 endometrial biopsies + 10 first-trimester + 16 term decidua + 18 labour samples, 0 paired across the non-pregnant/pregnant boundary; its scRNA-seq arm pooled 15 donors across 5 stages. Strunz 2021 bulk RNA-seq arm: 4 donors, 12 libraries (from deposited data only). Mouse lineage work (Sojka 2018): 6 decidualized horns from 2 independent parabiosis experiments (n=6 parabiotic pairs), plus gd6.5 n=4 and gd11.5 n=8, deciduoma n=10.
audit.n_unit: women (independent donors); 0 endometrium-decidua pairs from the same individual anywhere in the located human literature. Mouse figures are parabiotic pairs / animals. NOT cells.
audit.controls: Primary (Feyaerts 2024) controls are thin and the authors say so: NO paired within-woman control ("we had no access to paired samples, i.e. endometrial and decidual NK cells from the same individual"); NO peripheral-blood comparator reported in Materials and methods; NO KIR genotyping for the decidua donors ("we lack KIR genotyping results for the donors of the abortion material, preventing us from making adjustments"); NO age/parity/gravidity data for decidua donors (anonymous donation); menstrual blood used as an endometrium proxy that the authors concede has never been validated head-to-head against biopsy in the same individual; enzymatic-digestion epitope loss addressed only by citing prior work, not by an experiment in this paper. Note the two arms use DIFFERENT tissue sources and DIFFERENT isolation chemistries (RosetteSep/Ficoll on menstrual blood vs Accutase/gentleMACS/Percoll on decidua), which is uncontrolled. The one genuinely useful negative control in the corpus is in Whettlock 2022, which took matched peripheral venous blood from every donor and found pNK frequency and KIR/LILRB1/CD94 expression unchanged across all 7 stages — this makes a purely systemic/technical explanation for the uterine changes less likely, but says nothing about whether the uterine cells are the same cells.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: SELECTION/EXPANSION OF A PRE-EXISTING SUBSET, plus local proliferation — and it is not a hypothetical. All three uNK subsets (uNK1/uNK2/uNK3) are already present in non-pregnant endometrium at menstrual, proliferative and secretory phase (Whettlock 2022), so every reported "pregnancy-induced adaptation" is fully explained by differential expansion/attrition of pre-existing states under progesterone and IL-15 with no cell changing identity: the frequency of a state can rise without any cell converting into it. The mouse experiment that can actually distinguish these — Sojka 2018, Ncr1-iCre x Rosa-mT/mG reporter mice in parabiosis with experimentally induced deciduomata — comes down on the expansion side: "the accumulated uNK cells were proliferating trNK cells; migrating NK cells made no contribution." The 2026 mouse Tbx21-Cre fate map likewise concludes "subset redistribution", explicitly "rather than undergoing lineage diversion." Two further alternatives are live: (i) REPLACEMENT FROM CIRCULATION — Vacca 2011 (PMID 21248224) shows CD34+ precursors resident in decidua differentiate into NK cells on stromal contact, i.e. de novo local generation from precursors rather than from eNK, and Carlino 2008 (PMID 18187664) shows chemokine-driven recruitment of circulating NK through decidual tissue; (ii) TECHNICAL ARTEFACT — the primary study's "endometrial" cells are menstrual-blood-derived and its "decidual" cells are enzymatically digested tissue, so the KIR-down/NCR-up difference could be a sampling and digestion-epitope artefact. Nothing in the human record discriminates conversion from any of these, because no human cell has ever been followed across the boundary.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, and it is human and direct. Strunz B, Ivarsson MA, ... Björkström NK. "Reconstitution of the uterine immune milieu after uterus or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation." Sci Transl Med 2026;18(840):eadp2583, PMID 41811987 (abstract-only; closed access, methods not read — flagged as such): using SNP- and HLA-disparity-based single-cell assignment of donor vs recipient origin by scRNA-seq and high-parameter flow cytometry in women after uterus transplantation or HSCT, "Recipient-derived immune cells replaced donor immune cells after uterus transplant, whereas HSCT resulted in near-complete donor-derived immune reconstitution, including formation of tissue-resident lymphocytes," and in one patient male-origin cells reconstituted the endometrium. That is direct human chimerism evidence that the endometrial uNK compartment is continuously refilled from circulating precursors — i.e. the endometrial NK pool present in one cycle need not be the pool present in the next, let alone the dNK pool of a later pregnancy. The same group's 2021 abstract concedes the point ("the uNK cell niche could be replenished from circulation"). Second counter-line: Feyaerts D et al. 2019, Cell Mol Immunol 16:410-1, PMID 30635647 / PMC6462002 (10 nulligravidae vs 25 multigravidae, CMV-stratified) shows the "pregnancy-trained" NKG2C+LILRB1+ endometrial NK signature that Gamliel 2018 (PMID 29768178) used to argue eNK are dNK precursors is partly CMV-driven — "the increase of pregnancy-induced LILRB1 expression on NKG2C+ eNK cells only occurs in CMVpos and not in CMVneg women" — i.e. a confounder, not a pregnancy-lineage relationship. Third: Huhn 2020 (PMID 31959757), 41-marker CyTOF on 28 first-trimester decidua donors, "did not identify a cluster directly corresponding to 'pregnancy trained dNK cells' (PTdNK)." Note also that Gamliel 2018 itself only claims "The precursors of PTdNKs SEEM TO BE found in the endometrium." I searched specifically for a human study sampling endometrium and decidua from the same woman and found none; Feyaerts 2024 states such pairing "poses inconceivable logistic and ethical barriers."
audit.downstream_dependency: (1) CLINICAL PRE-CONCEPTION uNK TESTING. Non-pregnant endometrial biopsy CD56+ uNK density/percentage is offered commercially and in RM/RIF clinics to triage women to prednisolone, intralipid or IVIG. The entire diagnostic logic requires that the eNK measured in a luteal-phase biopsy are the cells that will constitute the dNK compartment of a future pregnancy — i.e. it is exactly claim S3. See the systematic review/meta-analysis of this literature, "Number and function of uterine natural killer cells in recurrent miscarriage and implantation failure" (PMID 35265977 / PMC9247428). If the compartment is instead refilled from circulation between the biopsy and the pregnancy (Strunz 2026 STM), the biopsy is not measuring the cells it is claimed to predict. (2) THE CROSS-STAGE uNK1/2/3 ATLAS. Whettlock 2022 applies the dNK1/dNK2/dNK3 labels — defined by Vento-Tormo et al. in first-trimester DECIDUA — to non-pregnant endometrial cells and then reports that "uNK1 and uNK2 peak in the first trimester" and that "uNK subsets upregulate KIR and LILRB1 during transition from non-pregnant endometrium to first-trimester decidua." Both are statements about one population changing over time and are only interpretable if S3 holds; otherwise they are statements about the relative abundance of unrelated populations in unrelated women. (3) THE PTdNK / TRAINED-MEMORY MODEL. Gamliel 2018 Immunity's proposal that pregnancy training persists in the endometrium between pregnancies and improves placentation in subsequent pregnancies (and the derived "learning from experience" framework, PMID 30802436) rests entirely on eNK->dNK continuity across the cycle-to-pregnancy boundary.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: The initial call INFERENCE is confirmed, not overturned — but it is too generous in two ways that the row should record. (a) It should be tightened to INF_MARKER specifically. There is no human observation of persistence or conversion at all: the primary source is an unpaired between-groups flow-cytometry comparison of 26 menstrual-blood donors against 14 decidua donors, and the authors state that paired sampling "poses inconceivable logistic and ethical barriers." Every supporting human study has the same architecture. There is no pseudotime/velocity claim to demote here, but the word "differentiation pathway" in the Strunz 2021 title denotes ordering of statically sorted CD39/KIR subsets, which is INF_MARKER dressed as INF_TRAJECTORY. (b) More importantly, INFERENCE reads as "unproven but unopposed", and that is wrong: the claim is actively opposed. The only parabiosis experiment in the field (Sojka 2018, mouse) attributes uNK accumulation at decidualization to local proliferation of a pre-existing tissue-resident pool with zero contribution from migrating NK; the 2026 mouse T-bet fate map calls the gestational change "subset redistribution ... rather than undergoing lineage diversion"; and human transplantation chimerism (Strunz 2026 STM) shows the endometrial immune compartment being replaced from circulation after uterus transplant and reconstituted donor-wide after HSCT. Each of these is compatible with dNK arising by selection/expansion or fresh recruitment rather than by eNK converting. The claim as worded ("eNK -> dNK") should be recorded as an untested precursor hypothesis that the field itself hedges (Feyaerts 2024: "It is hypothesized that NK cells in the endometrium are precursors for decidual NK cells"; Gamliel 2018: precursors "seem to be found in the endometrium"), not as an established transition. Distinct from S2: this row is only about the temporal non-pregnant->pregnant boundary, and that specific boundary has never been crossed by any labelled cell in any species.
audit.methods_quote: Feyaerts 2024, Materials and methods, Tissue sampling (verbatim, archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/S3_PMC10987737_METHODS_verbatim.txt): "Menstrual blood was collected from 26 healthy women during the first 36 hours of menstruation, as described earlier (4, 23). Decidual tissue from 14 women undergoing elective termination of normal pregnancy between 6 and 15 weeks of gestation was collected at the Mildred Clinic Arnhem (Arnhem, the Netherlands). Tissues from elective terminations were donated anonymously. As such, demographics information such as age and parity/gravidity is not available for these samples." // Discussion, limitations (verbatim): "Firstly, we had no access to paired samples, i.e. endometrial and decidual NK cells from the same individual. Paired samples would shed light onto the specific changes NK cells undergo in a single individual. However, this poses inconceivable logistic and ethical barriers." // Discussion, framing the claim as untested (verbatim): "It is hypothesized that NK cells in non-pregnant endometrium are precursors of decidual NK cells present during pregnancy." // Sojka 2018 abstract (verbatim, PMID 30275046): "In parabiosis studies using experimentally induced deciduomata, the accumulated uNK cells were proliferating trNK cells; migrating NK cells made no contribution."
audit.notes: SOURCE-LOCATION RESULTS, including negatives, per G3. (i) SEARCHED AND COULD NOT FIND: any human study sampling endometrium and decidua from the SAME individual (search: "paired longitudinal same woman endometrial biopsy prior to pregnancy and decidua uterine NK cells lineage" — returned only conference-abstract noise); any human lineage-tracing, barcoding, TCR/KIR-clonotype tracking, deuterium/BrdU labelling or in-vivo persistence assay spanning the cycle-to-pregnancy boundary. (ii) SEARCHED AND FOUND BUT UNREADABLE: Strunz 2021 Sci Immunol (paywalled, verified closed via Unpaywall API and Europe PMC core record; science.org 403). Strunz 2026 Sci Transl Med PMID 41811987 is also abstract-only in this environment; its counter-evidence value above is taken from the abstract and is labelled as such rather than presented as read methods. (iii) HINT VERIFICATION: the hint's framing that "in humans the two timepoints are almost never obtainable from the same individual" is confirmed and is stated in the primary source's own words — it is not merely a practical limitation, it is the reason the entire human evidence base is INF_MARKER. (iv) A material and under-reported design fact: the primary study's "endometrial NK" are MENSTRUAL-BLOOD-derived, not biopsy-derived, and the authors concede that a biopsy-vs-menstrual-blood comparison "preferably in the same individual, is still needed." (v) Archived full texts for this claim: /home/user/aaa/refs/S3_PMC10987737.txt, S3_PMC10987737_METHODS_verbatim.txt, S3_PMC9245422.txt, S3_PMC12961421.txt, S3_PMC6971012.txt, S3_PMC6552671.txt, S3_PMC6462002.txt, S3_33617461.txt, S3_41811987.txt, S3_29768178.txt.
